translationRepairs: Whenever an army commander's billet fell vacant, the post was filled by successive promotion from among army commanders-in-chief.
Whenever an army commander-in-chief's billet fell vacant, the post was filled by successive promotion from among army commanders.
軍主 (army commander-in-chief) vacancies were filled from 軍都指揮使 (army commanders); the translation reverses the two ranks.

The emperor, because they had long served in the military ranks, ordered them placed in the palace guards: those carrying nominal commanderies were given grand generalships, and those without nominal commanderies were given generalships.

The emperor, because they had long served in the military ranks, ordered them placed in the imperial guard generalships: those holding titular prefectures were made grand generals, and those without were made generals.
遙郡 are titular (nominal) prefectures and 環衛 the honorary imperial guard general posts; 'nominal commanderies' and 'palace guards' mistranslate them.
In Zhiping 1 seventy men of talent were selected from duty platoon senior attendants and Palace Guard deputy horse-and-arms officers and above, and the emperor inspected them personally at the hall.

In Zhiping 1 seventy men of talent were selected from duty platoon rank-and-file and Palace Guard deputy horse-and-arms officers and above, and the emperor inspected them personally from the throne terrace.
長行 are rank-and-file soldiers, not 'senior attendants'; 臨軒 means at the front terrace of the hall.

In the ninth year, as rank rotation approached, the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized: "Civil exchange is somewhat generous—officers who rise from the ranks with merit soon reach regimental training commissioner."

In the ninth year, as rank rotation approached, the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized: "Transfer to civil rank is somewhat generous—officers who rise from the ranks with merit soon reach regimental training commissioner."
換官 means transferring military officers to civil/other rank; 'civil exchange' is opaque.
Supplementary Rank-Rotation Regulations: "Sun-Bearing and Heavenly Martial army commanders without titular prefectships exchange for Left Treasury Commissioner and shed the titular prefectship;

Supplementary Rank-Rotation Regulations: "Sun-Bearing and Heavenly Martial army commanders without titular prefectships exchange for Left Treasury Commissioner and are also granted a titular prefectship;
仍除遙刺 means 'and are also appointed to a titular prefectship' (除 = appoint), not 'shed' it.

Also: "Gongsheng, Divine Valor, Valiant Cavalry, Cloud Cavalry, and Martial Display army commanders exchange for Literary Enterprise Commissioner and shed titular prefectship; those already holding it remain as before;

Also: "Gongsheng, Divine Valor, Valiant Cavalry, Cloud Cavalry, and Martial Display army commanders exchange for Literary Enterprise Commissioner and are also granted a titular prefectship; those already holding it remain as before;
仍除遙刺 means 'and are also appointed to a titular prefectship' (除 = appoint), not 'shed' it.
The Bureau proposed that Imperial Dragon and Inner Palace Duty adjutants, aside from civil exchange under regulation, all shed titular prefectship;
The Bureau proposed that Imperial Dragon and Inner Palace Duty adjutants, besides the civil exchange due under regulation, all be granted a titular prefectship;
並除遙刺 means all are appointed (除) to a titular prefectship, not that they 'shed' it.

Men who also served East-West Platoon, Scattered Duty, or Jung Rong Duty belonged to the near-lower platoon ranks, and their deputy directors likewise exchanged for Inner Hall Honored Attendant one grade below a director.

Men who also served East-West Platoon, Scattered Duty, or Junrong Duty belonged to the near-lower platoon ranks, and their deputy directors likewise exchanged for Inner Hall Honored Attendant one grade below a director.
鈞容直 is romanized Junrong, not 'Jung Rong'.

By Xianchun, great generals such as Lu Wende, Xia Gui, Sun Huchen, and Fan Wenhua traded on merit and imperial favor, were insolent to superiors and cruel to subordinates, treated rank-and-file merit rewards as private property, favored kin and old friends, let warriors die in the weeds while schemers sat and stole their honors and ranks.

By the Xianchun reign, great generals such as Lü Wende, Xia Gui, Sun Huchen, and Fan Wenhu traded on merit and imperial favor, were insolent to superiors and cruel to subordinates, treated rank-and-file merit rewards as private property, favored kin and old friends, let warriors die in the weeds while schemers sat and stole their honors and ranks.
呂文德 is Lü Wende (not 'Lu') and 範文虎 is Fan Wenhu (not 'Fan Wenhua').
Lu Yijian said: "Since Yuanhao rebelled, each border fort and camp had made its own plan to hold fast. If the enemy broke through in a rush, the capital region would be thrown into alarm.
Lü Yijian said: "Since Yuanhao rebelled, each border fort and camp had made its own plan to hold fast. If the enemy broke through in a rush, the capital region would be thrown into alarm.
呂夷簡 is Lü Yijian, not 'Lu'.
The armies of Dingzhou, Zhen Ding Prefecture, and Gaoyang Pass did not connect in deployment, so mobilization sent them crisscrossing one another to little effect.
The armies of Dingzhou, Zhending Prefecture, and Gaoyang Pass did not connect in deployment, so mobilization sent them crisscrossing one another to little effect.
真定府 is Zhending Prefecture, not 'Zhen Ding'.
The An Lushan rebellion arose because the capital was empty and treacherous ministers could indulge their will."
The Tianbao rebellion arose because the capital was empty and treacherous ministers could indulge their will."
天寶之亂 is literally 'the Tianbao disorder'; the source names no rebel, so 'An Lushan rebellion' adds a name not in the text.
Western route garrison troops rotated every two years, but the eastern route alone was limited to three; when relief did not come on schedule, some fell to miasma—the emperor was deeply pained.
Western route garrison troops rotated every two years, but the eastern route alone was limited to three; when relief did not come on schedule, some fell to miasma—I am deeply pained by this.
朕甚惻然 is the emperor speaking in the first person inside the edict; it is not narration about 'the emperor'.

In the fourth month of Jingkang 1, Zhong Shidao was made Grand Commandant, retaining his previous posts as military governor of Zhenyao Army and pacification commissioner for Hebei and Hedong; later he was additionally made co-manager of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

In the fourth month of Jingkang 1, Zhong Shidao was made Grand Commandant, retaining his previous posts as military commissioner of Zhenyao Army and pacification commissioner for Hebei and Hedong; later he was additionally made co-administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
節度使 here is the Song honorary military commissioner title, not a 'military governor'; 同知樞密院事 is co-administrator (deputy) of the Bureau.
